newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline ends off as supplies seen building.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline ends off as supplies seen building.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline prices cratered Friday on talk of increasing supplies and weakness in the cash markets, while forecasts of warmer temperatures in the U.S. Northeast weighed on heating oil and crude prices.
"We had a sell-off in the (U.S.) Gulf (cash) market, and there are cargoes of gasoline headed our way. That's enough to burst gasoline's bubble," said a dealer.
December gasoline ended off 2.00 cents a gallon at 66.92 cents. Gasoline cash prices in the U.S Gulf Coast fell sharply on refiner selling after prices spiked earlier in the week.
December crude ended off 24 cents a barrel at $24.17.
Gasoline supplies are seen building now that some refinery gasoline making units which had been shut by mishaps or scheduled maintenance are coming back on line, traders said.
Also, more than 100,000 tonnes of gasoline were seen heading to the United States after the arbitrage from Europe opened last week.

Meanwhile, Weather Services Corp forecasted a return to near normal temperatures Monday and Tuesday of next in the key U.S. northeast heating oil market, pressuring heating oil. December heat ended off 0.79 cent a gallon at 72.61 cents.
Dealers said Friday's expiry in December crude options drove crude towards the $24.00 strike price, helping crude maintain technical support while it was pressured by weakness in refined products.

Dealers said the market was testing points on the spot 20-day moving average in crude as support, with $24.00 to $24.10 cited, after nearby crude had crossed the average on Thursday. December crude's session low Friday was $24.00.
"Crude held up relatively well," said a dealer.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
